prompt: Top-down editorial still life for a jewellery ad, vertical 9:16 frame, the camera looking straight down at 90 degrees and close. The camera is exactly overhead: the card is a flat upright rectangle with parallel edges, never seen at an angle or receding; the sailor ring is a true circle, not an ellipse (last time the camera tilted and the card receded). The piece and the empty type area sit inside the central 4:5 window. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It is the clasp up close on skin, a much closer view than this picture: copy the clasp's construction and pose from it, never its framing, its skin or its size. Preserve the necklace exactly: a 50 cm chain, 4 mm wide, of elongated paperclip links (about 4 x 11 mm) in polished 18k gold tone. 1 thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across (about 14 mm opening, small push-pin nub, ribbed gate collar) and 1 short straight bar about 15 mm long set with 1 row of about 9 tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. No pendant, no other stones. Must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6-0.7x the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar. The bar's stones are one single line of nine or ten tiny pavé-set clear stones, so small and close that the bar reads as a fine glittering line, as in reference 2; never seven large round stones in claw settings (last time the bar was drawn with seven big claw-set brilliants). The ring's top carries the stepped flat-cut gate sleeve at 11 o'clock; there is no separate collar band under the nub. The clasp is built exactly as in reference 2: the left strand ends in one jump ring at the outer end of the stone bar; the bar lies across the upper left of the sailor ring with its single row of tiny stones facing the camera; the ring's flat-cut gate sleeve sits at about 11 o'clock; the barrel collar at about 1 o'clock carries the one jump ring that joins the right strand; the small push-pin nub points outward at 3 o'clock with two or three ribbed grooves just below it at 4 o'clock. Exactly two chain ends meet the clasp, never a third strand or a loose jump ring. Every link, the ring, the bar and every jump ring are the same polished 18k gold tone, never a silver-tone, white-metal or rose part. SCALE: the frame is about 9 cm wide; each link is the length of a grain of basmati rice and the sailor ring is a little larger than a one-rupee coin, about a quarter of the frame width. The clasp is small against its own chain, exactly as in reference 1: about eight paperclip links lie across the frame besides the clasp, each link about one eighth of the frame width; the sailor ring's outer diameter is no more than one and three-quarter links laid end to end, never two or more; the stone bar is about one link long and 0.6 of the ring's diameter (last time the ring grew to almost three links across). The referent touching the chain is her forefinger's tip: its pad is about 15 mm wide and the ring about 22 mm, so the ring is one and a half fingertips across, never two, and each link is a little shorter than her fingertip is wide (last time the ring was two fingertips wide). No coin and no rice in the picture. WORLD: a roka invitation, a thick ivory handmade card with soft deckled edges, completely blank, its only decoration a thin double-rule border of plain straight lines in muted saffron and oxblood foil, with no corner ornaments. Oxblood silk shows above the card across the top quarter of the frame. The necklace is wrapped once round the card like a ribbon, so on the face of the card its front strand runs dead straight and level across the full width of the frame a little above the middle, every link lying flat, and the closed toggle lies face up on that line right of centre, the stone bar threaded through the ring, posed as in reference 2 and turned so both strands leave it level. Both strands leave the clasp at exactly the same height and run as one dead straight horizontal line from the left frame edge to her fingertips, which press it flat to the card at that same height; it never rises, dips or bends at the clasp, and her fingers never pinch or lift it (last time the right half rose from the clasp to pinching fingers). The oxblood silk across the top and the strip of card just under it stay calm and empty for a headline; below the chain the card is smooth, bare and empty for a long way, for type set later. The tips of two fingers of a woman's right hand, light wheatish skin, short bare natural nails, enter from the right edge of the frame just above the line and rest on the strand near its right end, the forefinger's pad pressing one link flat to the card as if she has just drawn the ribbon straight; the fingers stay in the right fifth of the frame, clear of the clasp. CONTACT: every link casts its own small, sharp, true contact shadow on the paper where it lies; the ring and the bar cast crisp crescent shadows; the fingertips cast a soft true contact shadow where they press the strand. LIGHT, two sources, both soft: (1) one large soft warm window light from the left, evenly lighting the whole card; no sun shafts, no window-frame shadows, no light stripes or dark bands across the card; every shadow small and soft (last time hard sun shafts and a dark diagonal band striped the card); (2) one small hard specular kicker from behind right draws a bright edge along every link and puts one white catchlight in each tiny stone. Warm neutral 18k gold tone, a soft butter yellow as in reference 1, never orange, coppery or brassy; the card is cool ivory, not peach (last time the gold went orange on peach-graded paper). Natural film grain, real paper tooth. Full-bleed 9:16 photograph edge to edge; no letterbox bands, frames or panels. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark: no monograms, names, symbols, deity motifs or pseudo-script on the card or anywhere in the frame. No face, no eyes, no eyebrows. No rings, bangles or any other jewellery on the fingers. Exactly one product: this necklace is the only piece in the frame.
